mechanism_narrative: The continued decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT from t-3w to t-0w implies fewer commuting-linked trips and lunch-time errands. If that pattern persists, retail and recreation mobility should remain below its recent 4-week average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stay flat or decline further.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated and falls only slightly, people keep substituting home-based activity for discretionary outings. That substitution suppresses RETAIL_REC within one week and should keep it below the prior 4-week mean unless RESIDENTIAL drops back toward baseline.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +15 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises within 7 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +15 and unchanged WORKPLACES/TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES after prolonged weakness indicates reopening pressure and more in-person activity. If both series rise together, retail and recreation mobility should improve over the following two weeks as commuting and shopping co-move upward.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each rise by at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES post simultaneous week-on-week gains of at least 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: An upward break in PARKS mobility often precedes warmer-weather discretionary movement and companion visits to commercial areas. If PARKS improves from its current depressed level, RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks because outdoor activity and shopping trips share the same seasonal impulse.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -55 after being below -60
failure_condition: PARKS moves above -55 but RETAIL_REC remains lower than its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A narrowing gap between GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES implies more routine out-of-home trips for both essentials and work. That combined activity should spill over into discretionary errands, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 14 days even though GROCERY_PHARM becomes less negative while WORKPLACES is also less negative.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL continues to rise while PARKS and RETAIL_REC both remain depressed, households are reallocating time toward home and away from discretionary destinations. That pattern should push RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks because at-home substitution crowds out shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds +18 while PARKS stays below -55
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above +18 and PARKS staying below -55.

mechanism_narrative: A regime of gradually easing mobility restrictions shows up first in TRANSIT stabilization and then in retail visits. If TRANSIT stops falling and turns upward for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC should improve within one week as access constraints loosen.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT posts two consecutive weekly increases after a prior decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after TRANSIT rises for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rebound in GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES indicates a broad return of non-discretionary movement that usually spills into retail errands. When all three series improve together, RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks than over the prior four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES all rise week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES all post simultaneous weekly gains.
